tasks.title: Get the right visa or permit, and note its renewal rules
tasks.summary: Your employer usually sponsors a work visa for Korea. Confirm which category applies and when it must be renewed.

tasks.title: Check passport validity for South Korea
tasks.summary: Make sure your passport stays valid well past your entry date so the visa can be issued for the full term.

tasks.title: Get apostilles for birth, marriage, and diploma records
tasks.summary: Your diploma will likely need an apostille for the work visa. Order it early; it can take weeks.

tasks.title: Driving: local license, international driving permit, or both
tasks.summary: You plan to use transit, so this is optional. An international driving permit keeps the option open for your first year.

tasks.title: Give notice to your landlord
tasks.summary: Check your lease for the notice period (often 30 to 60 days) and send written notice.

tasks.title: Schedule the move-out walkthrough
tasks.summary: Book it for after the movers leave and take photos of every room.

tasks.title: Get your deposit back
tasks.summary: Give your landlord a forwarding address and a way to pay you while you are abroad.

tasks.title: Hand over keys
tasks.summary: Return every key and fob and get a written receipt.

tasks.title: Move day plan
tasks.summary: Plan the day around your flight, the movers' pickup, and your cat's travel crate.

tasks.title: Hire a licensed international mover and compare quotes
tasks.summary: Get at least three quotes for a small shipment from Seattle to Seoul.

tasks.title: Get transit insurance for shipped items
tasks.summary: Insure your electronics and sentimental items for their replacement value.

tasks.title: Choose sea or air freight in time
tasks.summary: Sea freight takes about 3 to 4 months, so it would need to leave by early December. Air freight (about a month) fits your timeline better.

tasks.title: Have someone or a virtual mailbox service hold physical mail
tasks.summary: Your parents in Seattle could receive mail, or use a virtual mailbox service.

tasks.title: Keep your home number alive for bank texts and get a local eSIM
tasks.summary: Move your US number to a low-cost plan for 2FA codes, and use an eSIM for data in Korea.

tasks.title: Packing plan
tasks.summary: Split items into ship, carry, sell, and donate. You are keeping clothes, electronics, and sentimental items.

tasks.title: First-night bag
tasks.summary: Pack toiletries, a change of clothes, bedding, chargers, and snacks for you, plus two days of food for your cat. Keep this bag with you.

tasks.title: Clothes for March in Seoul
tasks.summary: Early March in Seoul is still cold, often near freezing in the mornings. Pack a warm coat and layers for your first two weeks.

tasks.title: Carry-on for the trip to South Korea
tasks.summary: Keep your passport, visa papers, laptop, chargers, a Korean plug adapter, and a change of clothes in the bag that stays with you.

tasks.title: Pack what you are keeping
tasks.summary: Decide what ships and what travels with you: clothes, electronics, sentimental items. Keep fragile and valuable things with you.

tasks.title: Open-first box
tasks.summary: Label one box Open First with cleaning supplies, tools, a few dishes, and anything you need on day one.

tasks.title: Pet travel kit
tasks.summary: Pack a travel kit for your cat: an airline-approved carrier, food, bowls, vet records, and something that smells like home.

tasks.title: Gear for your hobbies
tasks.summary: Bring your taekwondo uniform and belt. Game accounts travel with you, so there is nothing to pack for Limbus Company.

tasks.title: Choose a location
tasks.summary: Compare Seoul neighborhoods within 40 minutes of Gangnam by transit and within your $1,400 monthly budget.

tasks.title: Check the commute to your pins
tasks.summary: See transit times from each candidate area to your Gangnam office.

tasks.title: Apply
tasks.summary: Have your passport, visa, and employment letter ready when you apply.

tasks.title: Review and sign the lease
tasks.summary: Check the deposit amount, monthly rent, maintenance fees, and the contract length before you sign.

tasks.title: Pay the deposit and get a receipt
tasks.summary: Deposits in Seoul can be large. Pay by traceable transfer and keep the receipt.

tasks.title: Set up utilities and internet
tasks.summary: Ask the landlord which utilities are included and book internet installation for your first week.

tasks.title: Change your address
tasks.summary: Update your address with banks, your employer, and government accounts.

tasks.title: Update your ID
tasks.summary: Keep your US ID valid; you will get a local residence card after arrival.

tasks.title: Proof of insurance
tasks.summary: Get renters insurance for your new place and cancel the old policy after move-out.

tasks.title: Banks and bills
tasks.summary: Cancel or transfer utilities and subscriptions, and plan how you will move money to Korea.

tasks.title: Papers in the bag
tasks.summary: Carry your passport, visa documents, apostilled diploma, lease, and your cat's health certificate. Don't ship them.

tasks.title: Cards that work abroad
tasks.summary: Use a card with no foreign transaction fees and tell your bank about the move.

tasks.title: A backup card from a different provider
tasks.summary: Carry a second card on a different network in case one is blocked.

tasks.title: Tax obligations in both countries
tasks.summary: US citizens still file US taxes while abroad. Learn what you will owe in Korea too.

tasks.title: Savings buffer
tasks.summary: Aim for moving costs plus 3 to 6 months of expenses: about $12,000 to $16,000 based on your budget.

tasks.title: Register for your residence card after arriving
tasks.summary: Long-term foreign residents in Korea register for a residence card soon after arrival. Book the appointment early.

tasks.title: Find a clinic near your new home
tasks.summary: Look for an English-friendly clinic near the area you choose.

tasks.title: Prescriptions
tasks.summary: Get enough of any prescriptions to cover your first months and carry the paperwork.

tasks.title: Medical records
tasks.summary: Request digital copies of your records and vaccinations.

tasks.title: Checkup before leaving
tasks.summary: Book physical, vision, and dental checkups while you still have US coverage.

tasks.title: A policy that covers care and evacuation in South Korea
tasks.summary: Bridge the gap until local coverage starts. Examples of providers include SafetyWing, Allianz, Cigna, and Aetna.

tasks.title: Pets: vet records, travel, import rules
tasks.summary: Your cat needs a microchip, vaccinations, and a health certificate before flying. Start with the import rules.

tasks.title: A contact rhythm for people who stayed
tasks.summary: Pick a weekly call time with your parents that works across the time difference.

tasks.title: Get a transit card
tasks.summary: Get a rechargeable transit card for the subway and buses on your first day.

tasks.title: Find a regular social spot
tasks.summary: A pho place, a spot for Limbus Company fans, or a taekwondo gym near your new home.

tasks.title: Find a grocery store
tasks.summary: Find the closest grocery store to your new home.

tasks.title: Find a pharmacy
tasks.summary: Find a pharmacy near your new home.
